entries.label: laptop
entries.summary: A portable computer with a built-in screen, keyboard and battery.
steps: Open the lid and press the power button.
Sign in with your account.
Connect to Wi-Fi from the network icon.
Save your work, then use Shut down before closing the lid.
cautions: Do not block the air vents while it is running.
tutorial_queries: how to use a laptop for beginners

entries.label: cell phone
entries.summary: A handheld device for calls, messages and apps.
steps: Press and hold the side button to wake or power it on.
Unlock it with your PIN, fingerprint or face.
Open an app by tapping its icon.
Press the side button once to lock the screen.
cautions: Keep it away from water unless it is rated for it.
tutorial_queries: how to use a smartphone for beginners

entries.label: keyboard
entries.summary: An input device for typing text and giving shortcuts.
steps: Connect it by USB cable or Bluetooth.
Place your fingers on the home row (F and J have small bumps).
Use Shift for capital letters and Ctrl with C and V to copy and paste.
Use Backspace to delete the last character.
tutorial_queries: how to type properly keyboard basics

entries.label: mouse
entries.summary: A pointing device that moves the cursor on the screen.
steps: Connect it by USB receiver or Bluetooth and switch it on.
Move it on a flat surface to move the cursor.
Left-click to select or open, right-click for a menu.
Use the wheel to scroll.
tutorial_queries: how to use a computer mouse for beginners

entries.label: remote
entries.summary: A handheld controller for a TV or other device.
steps: Check that it has working batteries.
Point it at the device and press the power button.
Use the arrow buttons and OK to move through menus.
Use the volume and channel buttons to adjust sound and channel.
cautions: Never mix old and new batteries.
tutorial_queries: how to use a tv remote control

entries.label: tv
entries.summary: A screen for watching broadcasts, streaming and video inputs.
steps: Plug it in and press the power button on the TV or remote.
Choose the input source (HDMI, antenna or app).
Connect to Wi-Fi to use streaming apps.
Adjust the volume and picture mode in Settings.
cautions: Do not place it where it can tip over.
tutorial_queries: how to set up a smart tv

entries.label: clock
entries.summary: A device for showing the time.
steps: Find the time-set knob or button (analog) or the Set button (digital).
Turn or press until the correct time shows.
Set the alarm with the Alarm button if it has one.
Replace the battery when it runs slow or stops.
tutorial_queries: how to set an analog clock

entries.label: bottle
entries.summary: A container for carrying drinks.
steps: Twist the cap anticlockwise to open it.
Fill it with the drink, leaving a small gap at the top.
Close the cap firmly until it clicks or stops turning.
Wash it regularly with warm soapy water.
cautions: Do not fill a plastic bottle with very hot liquid unless it says it is heat safe.
tutorial_queries: how to clean a water bottle

entries.label: cup
entries.summary: A small open container for hot or cold drinks.
steps: Check that it is clean and has no cracks.
Pour the drink, leaving space at the top.
Hold it by the handle and let hot drinks cool a little before sipping.
Wash it after use.
cautions: Hot drinks can scald. Test the temperature first.
tutorial_queries: how to make a cup of tea

entries.label: bowl
entries.summary: A deep dish for food or for mixing.
steps: Wash it before first use.
Use it for serving or mixing ingredients.
Check that it is microwave safe before heating food in it.
Wash it after use.
cautions: Hot bowls can burn your hands; use a cloth.
tutorial_queries: microwave safe bowls how to tell

entries.label: fork
entries.summary: A utensil with prongs for eating or lifting food.
steps: Hold it in your hand like a pen, with the prongs pointing down.
Spear or scoop the food.
Bring it to your mouth and take the food off with your teeth.
Wash it after use.
tutorial_queries: how to use cutlery properly

entries.label: knife
entries.summary: A blade for cutting food.
steps: Hold the handle firmly and curl the fingers of your other hand away from the blade.
Cut on a stable board with slow, controlled strokes.
Cut away from your body and never towards your hand.
Wash it by hand and store it with the blade protected.
cautions: Sharp. Keep it away from children and never catch a falling knife.
tutorial_queries: basic knife skills for beginners

entries.label: spoon
entries.summary: A utensil with a shallow bowl for eating, stirring and serving.
steps: Hold the handle between thumb and fingers.
Scoop the food or liquid.
Bring it to your mouth and sip or eat from the side.
Wash it after use.
tutorial_queries: how to use a spoon correctly

entries.label: microwave
entries.summary: An appliance that heats food using microwaves.
steps: Put the food in a microwave-safe container and cover it loosely.
Close the door and set the time and power level.
Press Start and wait for the beep.
Use oven gloves and open the lid away from your face; steam is hot.
cautions: Never put metal or foil inside. Do not run it empty.
tutorial_queries: how to use a microwave oven safely

entries.label: oven
entries.summary: An appliance for baking and roasting food.
steps: Choose the temperature and mode, then let it preheat.
Place the food on a rack or tray using oven gloves.
Set a timer and check the food near the end of the time.
Turn it off and let it cool before cleaning.
cautions: Surfaces and trays get very hot.
tutorial_queries: how to use an oven for beginners

entries.label: toaster
entries.summary: An appliance that browns slices of bread.
steps: Plug it in and set the browning dial to a medium level.
Put in the bread and push the lever down.
Wait for it to pop up and take the toast out carefully.
Empty the crumb tray regularly.
cautions: Never push metal objects into a toaster.
tutorial_queries: how to use a toaster

entries.label: refrigerator
entries.summary: An appliance that keeps food cold.
steps: Keep the door closed as much as possible.
Put raw meat on the bottom shelf and ready foods higher up.
Cover or box leftovers before storing them.
Clean it and remove old food regularly.
tutorial_queries: how to organize a refrigerator

entries.label: book
entries.summary: A set of pages with text or pictures.
steps: Look at the contents page to find the chapter you want.
Hold it open flat and read page by page.
Use a bookmark instead of folding the page corner.
Store it upright or flat, away from damp.
tutorial_queries: how to take notes while reading a book

entries.label: scissors
entries.summary: A hand tool with two blades for cutting paper, cloth and thread.
steps: Put your thumb and fingers through the handles.
Open the blades and place the material between them.
Close the blades smoothly to cut.
Close them and store them with the points covered.
cautions: Sharp points. Pass them handle first.
tutorial_queries: how to use scissors safely

entries.label: backpack
entries.summary: A bag carried on the back with two shoulder straps.
steps: Put heavy items closest to your back.
Close all zips.
Wear both straps and adjust them so the bag sits high on your back.
Use the chest or waist strap if it has one.
cautions: Do not carry more than about a tenth to a fifth of your body weight.
tutorial_queries: how to pack and wear a backpack properly

entries.label: umbrella
entries.summary: A folding canopy that protects you from rain or sun.
steps: Hold the handle and push the slider or press the button to open.
Hold it slightly in front of you into the wind.
Shake off the water and close it fully.
Let it dry open before storing it.
cautions: Do not use it in lightning or strong wind.
tutorial_queries: how to use an umbrella

entries.label: handbag
entries.summary: A bag for carrying small personal items.
steps: Open the zip or clasp.
Keep valuables in an inner pocket.
Carry it on the shoulder or in the hand.
Close it fully when in crowded places.
tutorial_queries: how to organize a handbag

entries.label: suitcase
entries.summary: A case with wheels for carrying clothes while travelling.
steps: Open it flat and place heavy items near the wheels.
Roll clothes to save space.
Close the zip and lock it if it has a lock.
Pull up the handle and roll it behind you.
cautions: Check the airline's weight limit before you travel.
tutorial_queries: how to pack a suitcase efficiently

entries.label: vase
entries.summary: A container for displaying flowers.
steps: Fill it about two thirds with clean water.
Cut the flower stems at an angle.
Place the flowers in the water and arrange them.
Change the water every two days.
tutorial_queries: how to arrange flowers in a vase

entries.label: chair
entries.summary: A seat for one person.
steps: Check that it is stable on all legs.
Sit back with your feet flat on the floor.
Adjust height and backrest if it has levers.
Do not tilt it on two legs.
tutorial_queries: how to adjust an office chair

entries.label: toothbrush
entries.summary: A brush for cleaning teeth.
steps: Wet it and add a pea-sized amount of toothpaste.
Brush all surfaces gently in small circles for two minutes.
Spit out the toothpaste and rinse your mouth.
Rinse the brush and replace it every three months.
tutorial_queries: how to brush your teeth correctly

entries.label: energy_drink_can
entries.summary: A sealed drink can. (Appears after you fine-tune a custom 'energy_drink_can' class.)
steps: Check the date and that the can is not dented or swollen.
Pull the tab up and back to open it.
Sip slowly and read the label for the serving size.
Recycle the empty can.
cautions: Energy drinks contain a lot of caffeine. Do not give them to children and limit how much you drink.
tutorial_queries: energy drink caffeine facts
